plain.li: [task,warm,winover,letter] Your last letter went from hand to hand here before it reached me, {WRITER}. Everyone wanted to read it.
[task,warm,winover,theirHightech] Good to hear from you again, {WRITER}. People here look forward to your letters more than they let on.
[task,cordial,winover,task:visited] It was good to put a face to the letters when you came. Write again soon.
[task,cordial,winover,theirLowtech] Your words were read out at our table, and our head asked to hear them a second time.
[task,cool,winover,theirLowtech] You write often, for a people we have met so seldom. We will see what comes of it.
[task,cool,winover,theirHightech] Received. We note your colony's interest. Further letters are welcome, though not required.
[task,curt,winover,call] You call a great deal, {WRITER}. Say what you need and let us get on.
[task,refusal,winover] Our head has read your letters and has no wish to answer them. Please stop sending them.
[task,refusal,winover,theirLowtech] We do not know you well enough for letters like these. Send fewer, or none.
[task,warm,trade,theirLowtech] Bring your goods to us and you will find buyers waiting at the stalls. Tell us what you make, and we will tell the market.
[task,warm,trade,theirHightech] Your list looks good to us. Our buyers have already marked a few lines on it.
[task,cordial,trade,call] Thanks for calling, {WRITER}. Our traders want to hear more about what you make.
[task,cool,trade,theirLowtech] Trade is trade. Our people will buy if your prices are honest, and not otherwise.
[task,cool,trade,theirHightech] We'll consider it. Your goods would have to beat what we already buy.
[task,curt,trade] We have traders of our own. Write again when you have something we can't get elsewhere.
[task,refusal,trade] We are not looking for new trade this season. Our caravans have enough to carry.
[task,warm,bringhome] The one of yours we hold is well, and asks after home. We would rather settle this than keep them.
[task,cordial,bringhome,theirHightech] Your colonist is in good health. We are prepared to discuss terms.
[task,curt,bringhome] We have them, and they are alive. That is all we will say until there is a price.
[task,refusal,bringhome,theirLowtech] Write all you like. The one we hold stays with us until we decide otherwise.
[task,refusal,bringhome] Your letters change nothing. We will name a price when we are ready.
[task,warm,theirkin] Thank you for word of our people. We will make an offer for them, and a fair one.
[task,cordial,theirkin,theirLowtech] We have told the families that our people are alive and fed. They ask us to bring them home, and we mean to.
[task,curt,theirkin] We know where our people are. We will make an offer when we can.
[task,refusal,theirkin] You hold our people behind bars and write to us of their comfort. Spare us the letters.
[task,warm,keepfaith,theirHightech] It's good to have neighbors who keep the same faith out here. Your letter was shared with everyone who came to the last service.
[task,cordial,keepfaith] Our people pray for your colony at each rite, as you pray for us. That is a bond worth keeping.
[task,cool,keepfaith] We share a faith, and that is something. It is not everything.
[task,curt,keepfaith] We have your letter. Our faith keeps itself.
[task,warm,speakfaith] We enjoy your letters even where we disagree with them, which is often. Keep writing.
[task,cool,speakfaith,theirLowtech] Our ways are older than your colony, {WRITER}. Letters will not change them.
[task,curt,speakfaith] We read it. We are not persuaded, and we would rather not be urged.
[task,refusal,speakfaith] Write to us of anything else, {WRITER}. Not of this.
[task,warm,host,theirLowtech] We will come to your feast with the best we have, and sit wherever we are put.
[task,cordial,host,theirHightech] We'd be glad to attend. Tell us the day and we'll arrange the travel.
[task,cordial,host,call] A feast? We'd like that, {WRITER}. Name the day.
[task,curt,host] Perhaps. It depends on the season, and on who else is asked.
[task,refusal,host] Our people have too much to do at home for feasting abroad.
[task,warm,dues] The dues are ready, and gladly given. Your protection has been worth them.
[task,warm,dues,theirLowtech] Our carter will bring the dues. Tell your council we have not forgotten what your colony does for us.
[task,cordial,dues] Our carter will bring the season's dues to your gate.
[task,cordial,dues,theirHightech] The dues are set aside for you. Our carter will bring them to your gate.
[task,cool,dues] You will have the dues. Our people paid them with tight belts.
[task,cool,dues,vassal:heavy] You will have your dues, on top of the harvest your colony already took from us.
[task,cool,dues,theirLowtech] The carter will come with what we can give. Our head asks you to remember it was given.
[task,curt,pressed,theirHightech] Payment is on its way. Consider this the last contact between us on the matter.
[task,curt,pressed,letter] The silver comes with whoever carries this. Count it, and forget my name.
[task,refusal,pressed,theirHightech] No. Tell whoever you like, and see what your neighbors think of how you came by it.
[task,refusal,pressed,letter] I read your letter once and burned it. You will get nothing from me.
[greetings,warm,us:task,task:visited,!task:you] We still talk of {OFFICER}'s visit here. Give {OFFICER} our regards, and tell them to come again.
[greetings,cordial,us:task:trade,task:you] Your questions about our trade have our traders talking, {WRITER}. Our greetings to your colony.
[greetings,cordial,us:task:trade,!task:you] {OFFICER}'s questions about our trade have our traders talking. Our greetings to your colony.
[greetings,cool,us:task,task:writes] Another letter from your colony. We have hardly answered the last.
[greetings,curt,us:task:speakfaith] We have your letter. If it is about your faith again, we have read enough of that.
[greetings,cordial,us:task:theirkin] Thank you for writing. Our families think of little but the ones in your cells, so any news of them is welcome.
[news,cordial,us:task:tend,!task:you] Here is our news, and the worst of it is the sickness. Tell {OFFICER} that anyone who comes with medicine is welcome.
[news,cordial,us:task:tend,task:you] Here is our news, and the worst of it is the sickness. Come when you can, {WRITER}, and bring what medicine you have.
[condolences,warm,us:task:keepfaith] We share your grief as we share your faith. Your dead will be named at our next rite.
[invitation,warm,us:task:host] We are promised to your feast already, and now to your gate as well. We will come.
[help,cordial,us:task:winover,!task:you] We send this gladly. {OFFICER}'s letters have made us feel we know your colony.
[help,cordial,us:task:winover,task:you] We send this gladly, {WRITER}. Your letters have made us feel we know your colony.
[warning,cordial,us:task:drill,!task:you] Thank you for the warning. Our fighters will be sharper for it, and sharper still once {OFFICER} has drilled them.
[greetings,cool,them:caughtkeeper] We have your letter, and we will read it more carefully than we used to.
[greetings,curt,them:pressed] Your letter came. After what your colony asked of me, I have little to say to it.
[news,curt,them:caughtkeeper] Here is our news. Your colony has gone looking for it before, so some of it you will know already.
[soundask,us] Walk with me, I've been meaning to ask about your people.
[soundask,us,theirLowtech] Who sits nearest your head's ear these days, would you say?
[soundask,us,theirHightech] Who really runs things back where you're from?
[soundask,us,kind] Come and sit, you look like you could use the rest.
[soundask,us,abrasive] You and I should talk, and you should do most of it.
[soundask,us,night] Can't sleep either, then, so sit with me.
[soundask,us,cold] Come in out of the cold and tell me how things are at home.
[soundtalk,us] Does your head listen to anyone, or decide alone?
[soundtalk,us] Strange, I'd heard the opposite.
[soundtalk,us] And what does the town make of that?
[soundtalk,them] Between us, not everyone at home is happy with how things are run.
[soundtalk,them] I've said more than I meant to already.
[soundtalk,them,theirLowtech] My own people wouldn't thank me for telling you this.
[soundtalk,them,theirHightech] That's not common knowledge, so keep it that way.
[soundtalk,them] Why do you want to know all this?
[pressyes,them] Not here, with people watching, but you'll have it.
[pressyes,them,theirLowtech] Take it, and may it sit heavy in your purse.
[pressyes,them,theirHightech] Fine, it's yours, and this conversation is over.
[pressyes,them,kind] I'll pay, though I thought better of you.
[pressno,them] Say it, then, I won't buy your silence.
[pressno,them,theirLowtech] My people will hear it from you, and remember who said it.
[pressno,them,theirHightech] Go ahead, I'd rather it was out than pay you for it.
[pressno,them,abrasive] You'll get nothing from me but this answer.
[keepercaught,them] I've known spies with better manners.
[keepercaught,them] You think I didn't notice where your questions were going?
[keepercaught,them,theirLowtech] My people will hear how your colony treats its guests.
[keepercaught,them,kind] I'd hoped your colony was better than this.
[keeperwatch,us] Someone ought to sit up with the guests.
[keeperwatch,us] Time I looked in on our visitors before they turn in.
[keeperwatch,us,cold] Cold night to be out, but the guests are still up.
[keeperwatch,us,rain] Wet night for it, but the guests are still awake.
[keeperwatch,us,lowtech] I'll take a lamp and see how our guests are settling in.
[keeperwatch,us,lowmood] Another late night with strangers, then.
[patrol,us,rain] Wet all the way round, and not a track worth following.
[patrol,us,snow] Only our own tracks in the snow out there.
[patrol,us,fog] Couldn't see far in the fog, but nothing came close.
[patrol,us,hot] Hot walk already, and the edges are quiet.
[patrol,us,lowtech] Walked the bounds, and nothing out of place.
[patrol,us,!lowtech] Perimeter's clear, all the way round.
[patrol,us] Nothing out there but wind and weeds.
[taskhome,us] Home, and it looks smaller than I remember.
[taskhome,us] Good to see our own gate again.
[taskhome,us] Back from the council's errand, and ready for a hot meal.
[taskhome,us,hurt] Home, a bit battered, but home.
[taskhome,us,rain] Home through the rain, and glad of it.
[taskhome,us,snow] Back through the snow, and my feet will never forgive me.
[taskhome,us,night] Home at last, and the place is fast asleep.
[taskhome,us,lowtech] The road home is always shorter than the road there.
[taskhome,us,!lowtech] Back, and I want a hot shower before anyone asks me anything.
[taskhome,us,lowmood] Home, and I'd rather not talk about the road.
[taskhome,us,highmood] Back, with plenty to tell the council.
